Hi Emily,

Appreciate the clarity — we can support this but there are two operational paths depending on whether you want the private offer terms changed (amendment) or prefer a billing-side split managed via the marketplace invoice mapping. Quick summary:

Option A — Amendment to private offer:
- Legal sign + DocuSign amendment to change SKU allocations on the offer (this updates the commit for reporting and affects how credits are consumed).
- Pros: explicit on the offer, easier to reconcile against the committed footprint.
- Cons: takes ~3–5 business days for legal + GCP partner approval.

Option B — PO/worksheet + invoice routing:
- We keep the private offer as-is and map the PO lines to separate billing entities. Finance sets invoice routing rules so charges for sku.ml.large hit the US entity and sku.ml.standard the EU entity.
- Pros: faster (1–2 business days for ops to configure), no amendment needed.
- Cons: commits remain aggregated on the offer (we can add internal allocation notes for your finance team).

For the escrow/credit release timing: we can configure a monthly drawdown with a 30‑day holdback for the first month, releasing 50% after the holdback period. I'll loop in Marissa (ops) and Jonas (co-sell/legal) below to confirm exact wiring.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to propose SKU mapping and invoice schedule (I attached a commit_matrix.xlsx to capture the mapping).
2) Jonas to confirm whether legal prefers an amendment or a PO-only approach for audit purposes.
3) Emily — confirm which option you prefer (amendment vs PO split) and if your AP needs specific invoice fields.

If helpful, I'm happy to set a 30‑minute call with Sam to validate the marketplace routing.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Global Partnerships (acting)
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Hi all,

I've drafted an operational plan below (Option B as the fast path). Please review and flag anything that would block AP.

SKU mapping (effective 2026-07-01):
- sku.ml.large: $120,000 (map to Avora Labs, Inc. — US billing entity)
- sku.ml.standard: $80,000 (map to Avora Labs Europe B.V. — EU billing entity)

Drawdown + invoice timing:
- Monthly drawdown on the 1st of each month; invoices generated on the 3rd.
- First-month holdback: 30 days after invoice date; release 50% of held credits on day 31, remaining 50% on day 60 (to match your cashflow request).

Required from Avora for ops setup:
- Confirm final PO numbers and indicate billing addresses for both legal entities (we need W‑9 equivalent for US).
- Confirm exact invoice header fields (PO #, cost center, VAT reg no for EU).

I've attached a basic invoice_schedule.csv with the proposed dates and a sample mapping row. Once we have PO numbers we can configure the marketplace invoice routing and send a test invoice to both AP teams.

If you prefer Option A (amendment), Jonas — what are the gating items / estimated timeline for legal?
